title: Characterization of Leukocyte-platelet Rich Fibrin, A Novel Biomaterial
protocol: Use licensed and certified professionals for all blood-drawing procedures.
Obtain approval from the Institutional Review Board or other appropriate authority for research involving human subjects.
Follow special precautions regarding informed consent and protecting participant identification.
Wear appropriate personal protective equipment at all times when handling human blood and/or blood products.
Dispose of waste according to biohazard regulations.
Identify the patient/participant and confirm with existing records.
Explain the study in detail and obtain an informed consent from the patient.
Set up a tray for each patient with tubes marked on a flat, stable surface.
Have the patient sit comfortably with their arm supported.
Inform the patient they will feel a small pinch and need to remain still during the procedure.
Attach the needle to the adapter.
Wash hands thoroughly and wear gloves.
Clean the antecubital fossa for venipuncture with 70% isopropyl alcohol in concentric circles from center outward.
Allow the cleaned site to air-dry for 30 seconds.
Identify the appropriate vein by palpation.
Apply the tourniquet 3-4 inches above the puncture site, ensuring it is not too tight (while still feeling the radial pulse).
Perform venipuncture by inserting the needle at a 15-30 degree angle to the skin in one smooth motion.
Push the blood collection tube through the needle and collect 9 ml of whole blood.
Remove the tourniquet.
Withdraw the needle from the patient's arm.
Apply gauze square over the puncture site prior to needle removal.
Dispose the used needle in an appropriate biohazard container.
Ask the patient to maintain pressure at the puncture site until bleeding stops.
Label the collected tubes properly.
Check the puncture site to ensure bleeding has stopped completely.
Apply adhesive bandage or tape over the gauze square on the puncture site.
Inquire if the patient is feeling alright, confirming no pain, swelling, or light-headedness.
Thank the patient before discharging them from the procedure area.
Place the blood collection tube immediately in a centrifuge after venous blood collection.
Centrifuge at 400 x g for 12 minutes at room temperature with an appropriate counter balance.
Remove the tube at the end of the cycle and observe the three layers: platelet-poor plasma (PPP), platelet-rich fibrin (L-PRF), and RBC base.
Aspirate the PPP layer using a pipette.
Gently pull out the L-PRF layer from the tube using tweezers.
Place the L-PRF clot in a sterile, perforated metal mesh.
Carefully scrape off the bulk of the red blood cell (RBC) layer using a surgical scalpel while leaving the buffy coat intact.
Gently compress the L-PRF clot for 30 seconds using a sterile metal plate with an approximate weight of 225 g.
Remove the plate and gently lift the L-PRF membrane.
Place L-PRF membranes on a filter paper for ease of handling.
Punch L-PRF membranes into “dog bones” using custom-made metal dies (2.75 mm wide at their narrowest point with a gauge length of 7.5 mm).
Measure the thickness of each sample at three spots and take the average.
Engage the L-PRF membrane in the center of the jaw grips of the uniaxial testing system.
Tear the filter paper support to expose the L-PRF membrane.
Program the instrument so that the movable head is operating at a constant rate (10.0 mm/min).
Record the elastic modulus, energy to break, and strain at break from the software accompanying the uniaxial testing system.
Place L-PRF membranes on a filter paper for ease of handling.
Cut L-PRF membranes into rectangular samples measuring 10 mm x 25 mm using a surgical scalpel.
Measure the thickness of each sample (average of 3).
Make a pinhole in the center of the sample using the stainless steel orthodontic ligature wire (220 µm in diameter).
Pass the ligature wire through the pinhole to form a loop and fix it to the tensile testing machine.
Place the edge of the L-PRF membrane to the lower jaw grip.
Program the instrument so that the movable head is operating at a constant rate of 10 mm/min.
Start the experiment.
Record the elastic modulus from the accompanying software.
Record the energy to break from the accompanying software.
Record the strain at break from the accompanying software.
Prepare L-PRF samples for SEM examination using a 10 mm dermal biopsy punch.
Place prepared samples in a 24-well plate.
Wash the samples with PBS.
Fix the samples with 2.5% glutaraldehyde (in PBS) for 20 min.
Dehydrate the specimens by immersion in 50% ethanol for 5 min.
Dehydrate the specimens by immersion in 70% ethanol for 5 min.
Dehydrate the specimens by immersion in 80% ethanol for 5 min.
Dehydrate the specimens by immersion in 90% ethanol for 5 min.
Dehydrate the specimens by immersion in 100% ethanol for 5 min.
Treat the samples with 0.5 ml of 100% HMDS (Hexamethyldisilazane) for 5 min.
Aerate the samples overnight to remove excess HMDS.
Mount the samples on stubs using a double-sided tape.
Sputter-coat platinum for 70 sec.
Examine the samples in a scanning electron microscope operating at an acceleration voltage of 20 kV (or appropriate setting).
Rinse membranes with PBS.
Soak membranes in 4 ml of 1% genipin solution (in 70% ethanol) for 48 hr.
Rinse membranes with PBS prior to experiments to remove excess genipin.
Place L-PRF membrane and genipin crosslinked L-PRF in 500 μl of 0.01% trypsin.
Incubate the samples at 37°C for 3 days with daily changes of trypsin.
Weigh the samples at day 1 prior to enzyme exposure.
Weigh the samples again at day 3 after incubation.
Heat PRF samples with 1 ml of 2% (w/v) ninhydrin for 15 min at 100°C.
Allow the heated solution to cool to room temperature.
Add 1.5 ml of 50% ethanol to the cooled solution.
Analyze absorbance at 570 nm using a suitable spectrophotometer.
Grow MC3T3 (mouse calvarial preosteoblasts) in Minimum Essential Medium –alpha modification (αMEM) until an 80% confluent monolayer is obtained.
Prepare fresh, sterile L-PRF membrane inside the cell culture hood.
Transfer the prepared L-PRF membrane onto a new cell culture dish.
Aspirate media from the flask.
Rinse the monolayer with PBS.
Add 5 ml of 0.05% trypsin and place the flask in a 37°C incubator for 5 min.
Pipette the contents of the flask into a centrifuge tube.
Centrifuge at 400 x g for 5 min.
Decant the supernatant.
Gently tap the tube to break the cell pellet.
Re-suspend with 4 ml of fresh α MEM.
Dispense a mixture of cell suspension (50 µl) and trypan blue (50 µl) into the hemocytometer.
Count the number of cells.
Seed 4x10^5 cells within 10 mm glass cloning rings placed on top of L-PRF membranes to retain the cells within the membranes.
Remove the rings after 24 hours.
Rinse constructs with PBS thrice for 10 min at day 4.
Add 1 ml of serum-free media and 200 µl MTS reagent to each well.
Incubate for 2 hr at 37°C.
Measure absorbance from 200 µl aliquots at 490 nm.
